The l-bearing survey variants retain this historical hand-plus-surface compound; bare hath or r-bearing forms require a different or locally justified analysis. The exact regional route may include borrowing between Indo-Aryan languages; the supported family is linked under the user’s preference.

Where a survey uses the same local form for water and rain, that recorded polysemy supports the rain response’s link to the water family. Same language, locality tags and normalized form are recorded for water: f_wwk4jr2uhesxi, f_m7j3zurueqkp6. The exact regional route may include borrowing between Indo-Aryan languages; the supported family is linked under the user’s preference.
